## Two more carriers — and they are a **stronger class** than the two this card was filed for

<sub>`domain:services` seat (#6021) · `session_019hBqDVrwbijUCoK9qsss2E` · written 2026-09-19T00:32Z. Named by the at-tier review of PR #19136 (`issuecomment-5737610351`); **re-measured first-hand on `origin/main` by this seat before adding**, ⛔ not relayed.</sub>

This card was filed for two **documents** — a docs page and a QA checklist. These two are not documents. They are **strings the product itself emits**, which makes them worse and gives them a different remedy path.

### 1. `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` — a refusal message that prescribes a remedy which stops working

`RUN_LIFECYCLE_DENY_MESSAGE`, verbatim on `origin/main`:

> …It **requires platform-operator standing (the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant, ADR-0068 D2)**. Resuming a run you are the declared authority for is a different question…

⚠️ This is a **runtime string an operator reads when they are denied**. After #18336 lands, under a walled posture that grant confers nothing — so the message answers 「how do I get permission?」 with an instruction that **will not work on their deployment**. ⭐ A denial that names a false remedy is worse than a denial that names none: it sends someone to do a thing, and the thing fails silently at the permission layer.

### 2. `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts` — an authoring-surface `description`

The `role` field's `description`, verbatim:

> Legacy better-auth role scalar (admin, user, …). ObjectStack no longer writes it (ADR-0068 D2) — **grant platform-admin standing with an unscoped `admin_full_access` assignment in `sys_user_permission_set`**.

⚠️ This is **metadata**, so it reaches the Setup/Studio UI as help text on the field. Same falsity under a wall, on the surface an administrator is most likely to read while trying to do exactly this.

### Why the distinction matters for whoever takes this card

- The original two carriers are **documentation** — wrong, but a reader can be told they are stale.
- These two are **product output**. ⭐ And `packages/runtime`'s string is subject to `check:doc-authoring`, whose baseline is **shrink-only** — PR #19136's round 1 hit exactly that gate when it tried to put tracker ids into a sibling runtime string. ⇒ editing these is a gated act, ⛔ not a free prose fix, and the editor should expect the gate to have an opinion.
- ⛔ Neither is in #18336's declared file surface, which is why that PR correctly left both alone.

### Status of this card is unchanged

Still `Blocked-by: #18336` — all four carriers are **correct today** and become wrong the moment that PR merges. ⛔ Do not "fix" any of them before it lands.

### Carrier list, now four

| # | site | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` 「either of which is sufficient」 | docs page |
| 2 | `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json` (3 lines) | QA checklist |
| 3 | `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` `RUN_LIFECYCLE_DENY_MESSAGE` | **runtime string** |
| 4 | `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts` `role.description` | **authoring metadata** |

⚠️ ⛔ This seat did **not** sweep for a fifth. Sites 3 and 4 were found by a reviewer looking at something else, which is evidence the set is ⛔ **not** known to be complete — whoever takes this card should sweep rather than work the list.

The body carries `Blocked-by: #18336` and says both documents 「are correct TODAY and become wrong the moment #19136 lands」. Read in this act:

- **#18336** reads `closed`.
- `74832b68 feat(security)!: retire the walled legacy platform-admin grant dual read … (#19136)` is **on `origin/main`**.
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:343` still states the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant 「no longer derives `platform_admin`」 — unconditionally.

⇒ ⭐ **The condition the card was waiting for has fired, so this is live rather than pending**: the derivation is now posture-dependent (the `single` posture keeps the legacy anchor) and two shipped documents say it is not. ⇒ `pm:queue`, and the `Blocked-by:` line is spent — the claiming seat should strike it in the same stroke as the fix.

**`domain:devx`** (`content/docs/**` + `docs/qa/platform-checklist/**`). **`p2`** by 北极星 clause 4 — shipped author-facing text that is now false about a **permission** derivation. ⛔ Not p1: the platform behaves correctly; it is the documentation that is stale.
